summary: # Ten-Minute Introduction Tutorial - Leather Jacket ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will go through the steps to create a leather jacket using Marvelous Designer. We will cover everything from adding a background image to creating and arranging patterns, sewing lines, and applying fabrics. ## Adding a Background Image In the window of 2D, right-click and choose to **add a background image**. Add the attached version to the background image. ## Drawing the Outline 1. Select the **multidirectional tool** and click along the background image to draw the outline. 2. Press **Ctrl** and click to draw the curve point. 3. Release **Ctrl** and click to re-create the curve point. 4. Click the starting point again to complete the creation of the outline. ## Creating Symmetrical Versions 1. Select the front and sleeve versions and press **Ctrl D** to create a symmetrical version. 2. Use the **edit version tool** to select the middle version and the back middle line. 3. Then, select the symmetry function in the menu through right-click. 4. Open the arrangement point and arrange the version on the map arrangement point. The sleeve version needs to be arranged on the outside of the arm. Since the back is a complete version, please place it on the back arrangement point. ## Adjusting the Versions 1. Press **Ctrl** and click to re-create the curve point. The back and sleeve versions do not need to be simulated at the moment. 2. Use the **position tool** to move the front right to the left front side to prevent collision. 3. Use the **sewing tool** to sew the outside of the version together. Please confirm that the sewing line length is correct. ## Creating Sewing Lines 1. Select the **M-B-N free sewing line** in the sewing line menu to create a sewing line between multiple sewing lines. The method of using the tool is similar to free sewing. 2. Click once from the right side of the sleeve in the order shown in the video. Finally, click the starting point again to complete the selection of the first set of lines. 3. Press **Enter** to confirm that the first set of lines has been selected and completed. Then, repeat the action to complete the second set of lines. ## Simulation and Line Details After opening the simulation, you can see that the sewing line on the sleeve is located on the right side. In this way, the sewing line on the side is hidden in the elbow position. ## Creating the Collar 1. Create an inner line to fold the collar. The fold angle will be increased to more than 180 degrees. The panel will fold inward along the inner line position. 2. The printed front panel will help the collar fold neatly. 3. Press **W** to click on the costume. The costume can be created with a fixed needle. You can adjust the arrangement position by moving the fixed needle. ## Adding Buttons 1. Select the button to create a button and click on the corresponding position on the panel. 2. Use the option to move the button to copy and paste the button. When pasting, press the right button to enter the specific number. 3. Click on the button inside to refer to the wrong button image. Please check your distance points to figure out which button is correct. ## Finalizing the Collar 1. After you’re done with the collar, press **H** to crack open your Aub sectors. 2. After you finish the sleeve, press **H** and hold down. 3. At this moment, activate the collar and sew it to the collar seat. 4. Then select to add to the outside to arrange the plate. If the collar is not stable, you can harden the plate. ## Adjusting Properties 1. Make its attribute hardening faster and more stable. After stabilizing, remove hardening. 2. Use a free sewing tool to sew the collar and the collar seat together. ## Applying Fabrics 1. Make the leather slide-down lambskin fabric and drag it to the fabric used to change the fabric. 2. Choose a color in the color palette or select a color with the color dispenser. 3. In the **Hardware and Trims** folder, you can load the shoulder pad or other accessories to the work area. ## Positioning Accessories 1. Use the **positioning ball tool** to move the shoulder pad to the shoulder area. 2. The cold shoulder pad pieces will be fixed in 3D space. Set their hierarchy to negative numbers to allow them to be worn externally. 3. Hide the cover for easy confirmation that the shoulder pad fits the body. ## Simulation and Adjustments 1. Activate simulation to ensure the shoulder pad fits correctly. 2. Choose the inner part of the supervising layer to create the Trevor estate. 3. Remove the joints of the baseboard pieces and set them as symmetrical pieces. ## Final Adjustments 1. Add a fixing needle to the corner of the collar. 2. Select the panels on the outer layer and modify the shrink rate to 101% to create a fold on the outer layer through the difference in size. 3. Reduce the particle diameter to 8 to achieve more detailed folds. 4. Add an elastic band to create a more realistic embroidered panel effect. ## Creating an Elastic Band 1. Measure the total length of the elastic band, then create a rectangular panel based on that length. The height of the rectangular panel is 10 mm. 2. Create a symmetrical elastic band panel and sew it to the main panel. The length of the elastic band should also be 10 mm. ## Addressing Panel Issues Sometimes, when you use the add-to-side tool, the panel will move to the wrong side. Re-activate the sleeve panel and hide them. Check if the elastic band panel is only attached to the sleeve side. If not, please click the add-to-side function again. ## Final Steps When the elastic band is in the correct position, sew the side line together. Increase the conflict thickness of the elastic band so it will be elastic along the seam line. Apply a new fabric type to the elastic band and change the physical properties of the fabric to "Trim for Green Leather." ## Conclusion The fabric has a very high bending strength, making the elastic band completely wrinkle-free and very hard. Due to the anti-activation of the sleeve version, the elastic band may have a small part in the sleeve insertion. The outer layer version sets the layer of the sleeve version as 1. The straps are set to 5.6 mm and the height to 0.6 mm, which is about 1.5 cm. Activate the simulation again. The elastic band will lift up the sleeve, and the seam allowances will be more obvious. Thank you for following along this tutorial!
